description:
Trigger: any /query call with a non-null filter or sort against MemoryBackend. memory.rs:566-614 signature accepts filter: Option<&O::Filter> and sort: Option<&[O::Comparator]> but the function body discards both with _filter and _sort. It then returns all object ids in ascending id order.

Actual bad behavior: clients running { "filter": { "relatedType": "Email" } } against this backend get every object back, not just the Email-related ones. The handler's cross-field validation (validate_metadata_filter) only rejects relatedIds-without-relatedType — it does NOT reject a non-trivial filter. So the test 'query_related_ids_with_related_type_passes_validation' in metadata.rs:1260 says 'validation passed, generic handler ran' and asserts no invalidArguments error — but the generic handler's result is wrong: it runs query_objects which silently ignores the filter.

This means the integration tests do not exercise actual filter semantics against MemoryBackend; only the cross-field VALIDATION path is covered. There are NO tests asserting Metadata/query with relatedType=Email actually returns only Email-related objects. The MemoryBackend is documented (memory.rs:5-18) as 'reference implementation' which downstream contributors will study. A contributor reading this implementation as documentation would see no filtering logic and might conclude the workspace doesn't require filtering.

Two bugs in tension here:
(a) Functional gap: MemoryBackend does not implement /query filtering. This is presented as a 'reference implementation' in module docs (memory.rs:5-13) and explicitly does NOT disclose the filter gap in the 'Metadata-specific behaviour' section (memory.rs:26-41) — it only discloses maySetPrivate/quota/related-validation.
(b) Test gap: nothing in the integration tests catches this.

Fix direction: either (i) implement basic filter and sort in MemoryBackend (matches §3.4 spec floor) or (ii) explicitly document the filter+sort no-op in the module-level rustdoc 'Metadata-specific behaviour' section so it is as loud as the other limitations.

Probe (do not run): write an integration test that creates two Annotations (Email-related and Mailbox-related) and calls Metadata/query with filter={relatedType:Email}, then asserts ids.len() == 1. Currently it would return 2.
title: MemoryBackend.query_objects ignores filter and sort, silently returning all objects
